text:
maria: noticing a new regression on canary — large dashboards (8+ tiles) are stalling on initial paint, CPU main thread spikes, then everything recovers after ~6s.

kevin: seen that in prod too? or only canary?

maria: only started after yesterday's routing policy change (route_affinity tweak). Canary traffic shows way more duplicated chunk downloads in network tab.

jess: can you paste a HAR or a quick repro?

maria: here's a small repro (open dashboard -> click timeseries -> pan) — captured trace + network: https://redwood-internal/artifacts/trace/1768123456 (private). main takeaway: same chunk file fetched 3x with slight query param diffs (`?v=1.0.3`, `?v=1.0.3&pf=true`) and hydration tries restart.

ryan: that sounds like prefetch client adding a fingerprint param when it gets rerouted? we changed prefetch route fallback to go to the cheapest region when affinity misses.

kevin: if prefetch runs then the real nav loads a different route and the client treats it as new chunk — hence duplicate download + parse thrash.

jess: can we disable prefetch on canary quickly?

maria: trying a hotspot toggle now: toggling PREFETCH_ENABLED=false for the canary route. pushing patch.

rollout-bot: rollout started for feature PREFETCH_ENABLED=false on canary (canary cluster: canary-eu-1)

kevin: any telemetry we can watch while the toggle is on? looking for main_thread_ms and chunk-download-count per session.

maria: watching telemetry: session_delta main_thread_ms drops from median 1600 -> 420, chunk_download_count per session drops 6.8 -> 2.1. firstpaint still a bit high but much less stutter.

ryan: so root cause: prefetch misrouted to fallback path that adds query param. That implies our routing layer should normalize asset requests or prefetch should use canonical asset URLs.

jess: agreed. short-term fix = keep PREFETCH_ENABLED=false for canary until we either: 1) make prefetch use canonical urls (no pf param) OR 2) change routing fallback to preserve original Host/URL.

kevin: which is less risky? 2 seems infra heavy and might touch CDN behavior. 1 is client change localized to console bundle. but we need tests to prevent this regressions in rollouts.

maria: I'll open a PR to strip client-side prefetch query params and add an integration test that runs prefetch+nav with a simulated routing fallback.

ryan: also add a telemetry gauge: chunk_dup_per_session and a regression alert if > 2.5 on canary/prod. current spike was 6.8 which is nasty.

jess: also add a lightweight liveness check for hydration restarts: detect when the same component unmounts+remounts within 5s during initial load and emit span.

rollout-bot: rollout succeeded for feature PREFETCH_ENABLED=false on canary (completed)

maria: quick notes for the fix PR: 
- change prefetcher to call getCanonicalAssetUrl(assetPath) before request
- add unit tests for query param normalization
- integration test: spawn routing fallback, assert only one GET for chunk-id X
- add console telemetry alert: chunk_dup_per_session

kevin: can you also check Dedicated customers? we had a few reports from a large customer but couldn't repro earlier. if their routing has similar affinity misses it might hit them.

maria: will run the instrumentation on a dedicated seat. if we see the metric bump we'll plan an emergency patch for dedicated instances too.

ryan: long term: routing layer should expose an option to preserve original asset URL headers (X-Original-Host) and CDN should strip the prefetch flags, but that's a bigger infra project. logged RFC: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/keep-assets-consistent-176812

jess: OK let's keep PREFETCH_ENABLED off on canary for 24h and monitor. if stable we can promote a minimal client fix to prod tomorrow.

maria: sounds good. I'll follow up with PR link and add the canary telemetry dashboard panel. thanks folks :thumbsup:

kevin: thanks. saving the trace to incident bucket in case we need to postmortem.

maria: (post-action) PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4891 — title: \"prefetch: normalize asset urls to prevent duplicated chunk downloads on routing fallback\"

ryan: nice. assign reviewers from eng-platform + eng-runtime.

jess: marked for quick review. once merged let's coordinate a small canary rollout with PREFETCH_ENABLED=true + fix enabled, so we can measure delta.

maria: will do. thread closed once we confirm 24h stable monitoring.
